raw_comment: The first thing that I noticed when looking at this graph was that the biggest word was gas, mentioned a total of 904 times. I figure that out of all of the words that were depicted in this visual, that is the one that may have had the most universal impact on the people surveyed. Gas is necessary to commute anywhere with a motor vehicle, whereas some other words that were mentioned in the visual do not have the same level of necessity and lack of substitutes. I noticed that food items were colored orange and that they made up the majority of the goods mentioned, with milk, meat, and beef as the top three foods. I wonder how this survey was conducted, like what groups of people they decided to survey. I wonder how the survey and the most mentioned words would look depending on different socioeconomic groups. I wonder what the visual would look like if it was organized based on the actual impact that inflation had on the price of the good. I imagine that although some of the products mentioned might not have had the highest overall price change due to inflation but rather the most used products make it so people are more likely to notice.

2. I wonder why bacon, hamburgers, and hair cuts are in such high demand. 
I wonder what other countries that deal with inflation or demands look like.

3. This is related to me and my community because demand here is important and without keeping that up it could be a problem as things getting shipped here does take some time so if something is in high demand it could be a problem for example vegetable oil was a big problem a while ago as demands were high but there were little to no vegetable oil and so inflation happened and the prices of fast food skyrocketed making fast food cost about 17-20$ a plate. 

4. What's going on with this graph? The graph is saying the differences of the high prices due to all that is going on in the world at the moment. A catchy headline is “The undying thirst of resources”

I notice that I’m not the only one that seem to be surprised by the gas prices nowadays. I also notice that there are more food products on the word cloud than there are non food products.

I wonder what type of items received less than 7 responses. I also wonder why the prices of milk, eggs, and meats have been on the rise.

This relates to me because locally the gas prices have been extremely high and I’ve heard from family members and friends that their gas prices have been even higher than what we have. For example in Hawaii the gas prices are around the $5 per gallon range but in California it’s over $7 per gallon. 

Headline: What’s The True Value of Products Nowadays?

Thoughts after the reveal: It seems that inflation in prices of most of the products is because of the war in Ukraine. I would understand why gas would be inflated but it surprises me that meats and dairy products are also being affected by the war as well.

It shows that there is a real supply and demand component to every aspect of our economy. A catchy title for the graph I think would be "Supply and Demands, the effects of Inflation"

raw_comment: In this graph, I notice that gas was the product that stood out most to people. Covid and everything going on with the world today has ruined a lot of different countries economies. There is such a large demand for the basic necessities but a supply shortage for all of these products. Milk, meat, beef, chicken, and eggs are all greatly consumed products in the world and so there is a huge demand for these foods because we live in a time where no one knows what will happen next. Recently, specifically within the last month, gas prices have grown higher than ever. This is because of the war between Ukraine and Russia. I wonder how long it is going to take for the gas prices to go down after the war ends. I also wonder if the crisis in Ukraine is going to affect products like milk, meat, etc., harsher in the next few weeks. This affects me and my community because I see these prices every day and I have to pay for these prices. A catchy headline is "Product Prices Increasing, Supply of Products Decreasing!"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
The first thing I noticed, or that caught my eye, was the fact that some words were in different colors and how next to each word are numbers ranging from highest to lowest (top to bottom).  

What do you wonder?
I wonder why there are certain items that aren't higher on this survey than others. For example, the price of shoes have skyrocketed recently. I also wonder why cars is on there twice.  One of the answers on this survey is also everything.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because me and my family have seen many of these products go up in price and we need a lot of these items as necessities.

What's going on in this graph?
In the graph we see various items that have been going up in price and I think this is happening due to how frequently they are being used and bought. 

Headline: The Price Is Wrong

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that these are all goods listed in order of how many times they are mentioned. I also notice how the colors of the words are either orange or grey depending on if they are a food item or not.  I then notice the little numbers next to each item. The caption on the bottom of the infographic says that the numbers show how many people mentioned each item.
What do you wonder?
I wonder what questions the people were asked that they mentioned these items? Was the topic on inflation and thats why gas was mentioned so much? Affordability? 
How does this relate to you and your community?
If I was asked on what consumes most of my money nowadays my answer would definitely be gas. As I am dependent on my parents for groceries I wouldn't have these specific answers but I spend a lot of money on food and I have noticed the raising prices. 
What's going on in this graph?
"Whats on the shopping list today?"

raw_comment:
I notice how gas is the word that most people mentioned. I also notice how beef products (beef, hamburgers, and ground beef) make multiple appearances. I thought it was interesting that so many people mentioned that. 

I wonder how this survey was conducted. Did each person give one word? or was it more like saying the first five products that came to mind?

raw_comment:
The first thing that I noticed was that the words in the orange are the consumables such as food and drink. As you can see is that it takes up about half of the entire list so therefore our daily day will usually start and end with some of us buying some of these products on the list. 

I wonder what causes these things to have higher prices or what causes these prices to go up. Is it inflation? Or are these items becoming more scarce?

This relates to me and my community because like I said before there are a lot of people that start and end their day with these products and that's only on the food side of the list. Stuff like rent, utilities, appliances, used and new cars, and insurance are all necessary and sometimes priority to live. The price of all these things getting higher really affects everyone. 

A catchy headline could be "The Effect of Inflation on the Daily Life".

1. What I noticed first was the size of the words. They are being ranked by what prices have stood out the most and the ones that do literally stand out the most in the article. I also noticed that everything orange is related to food/drinks.

4. In this graph a group of people took a survey in which they listed what products that the increase in prices stood out to them the most. Title: The Consequences of Inflation

raw_comment:
The first thing that I noticed was that some of the words are in different colors. Why is that? The second thing that I noticed were the numbers next to each word. More specifically, the word gas is practically double the amount of respondents versus any of the other words. This is probably due in part to the current global crisis going on. Another main takeaway that I have is that milk and other important foods that come from animals are typically the highest on the list. What does that say about animal products? Are grocery stores going to keep raising their prices? 

This affects me and my community because my family needs some of these goods to survive each day.

Headline: The Price isn't Right, survey says

I definitely have more questions about this graph than in previous ones. To begin, what are the demographics of the respondents? How old or young are they? Going off of that, how could that affect the results? I also wonder why they chose to use the font, font color, and how they chose to format their results.

raw_comment: While looking at this graph, I noticed that the words in grey represent common everyday purchases while the orange words represented food items. I also noticed little numbers on the bottom right of each word. Looking closely, you can see that the larger the number is, the bigger the word gets. I suppose that this means that the bigger words are the more common products purchased. I wonder why shampoo is orange. Was this simply a graphing error? If so, how trustworthy is this graph? Humans do not eat shampoo. I also wonder why milk is the second-largest underneath gas prices. I also can't believe that meat and beef have a large enough number to each be represented on their own. Finally, I wonder why the person who made this graph decided to separate the results into two groups with two different colors. Could it be to show how prevalent of a purchase that food is?   This relates to me and my community because this graph provides an accurate depiction of my family's day-to-day and year-to-year purchases. A good title for this graph could be "Big Words- Big Spending"

raw_comment: The first thing I noticed is the biggest one which is gas. Gas is a very big topic especially now as processes are and will continue to go up with the current conflict involving Russia. It is not surprising that almost a thousand people put the gas down. Milk, meat, beef, and chicken are the next couple of big words that a majority of people put. This is probably because they are staples in many households. When these staples' prices go up, people are more likely to notice the prices are going up for something they buy consistently and constantly. You can see the further you look and the fewer people put the word down, the more specific the wrod gets. If there were more general categories given I wonder how that would affect the results. I think a good name for this graph would be, "Supply and Demand Noticed".

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who responded.   We’re not publishing headlines now since the American Statistical Association (ASA) is running the 2022 Spring Headline Challenge.  But, some of the best headlines will be published in Friday’s Reveal that will appear below today’s graphs and instructions.

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back by Friday, April 1 to see the Reveal with the free link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graphs, and a few Stat Nuggets.

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).

View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex). 

Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who has been “opting-out” of many non-essential products and services due to increased prices, and David Wilcox of Lawrenceville, New Jersey, who has realized in the past year that many goods and services are non-essential.

I also notice there is a large difference between gas and milk, the second most-named product with higher prices. The difference between gas and milk is 449 people. I see lots of meat in the highest-raised products which makes me want to learn why meats specifically are getting more expensive. This graph relates to me and my community because the prices of all the products listed in the graph are bought by my family and the high prices affect our lives in many ways. The increased prices make it more difficult to constantly buy these needs which are crucial in our everyday lives like gas, food, cleaning supplies, etc. A headline that summarizes this graph is, "Increasing Prices of Everyday Items."

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?

   In regards to the graph, I notice that all of the first-tier products are critical, particularly those that are in high demand and short supply at the moment. Additionally, some words are highlighted in orange, while others are gray. The orange words appear to be all about food, whereas the gray words are not.

2. What do you wonder?

   In terms of this graph, I wonder why new and used cars are classified separately. I'm also curious as to why certain products were classified as food whereas others were not. For example, while dog food, pet food, and oil are not considered food products, shampoo is. I'm surprised at the total number of people who responded "everything," given how true that is due to inflation.

3. How does this relate to you and your community?

   This relates to me and my community in regards to inflation. Gas is a significant topic and issue that the entire country is dealing with. This is also prevalent among my own friends and family, when it comes to what products or every-day activities cost the most and are necessary, regardless of inflation. 

4. What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

   A catchy headline is: How Is Inflation Perceived?

raw_comment: I noticed that there were no answers that had a singular person who responded with that answer. raw_comment:
What's Going on in this Graph? - Higher Prices

1. The graph is a list of products that people surveyed said have increased in price. Food items are orange, and other items are black. Next to each item is the number of people that mentioned the item. Gas has the highest count by far at 904 responses. Every item listed has at least 7 responses.

2. I wonder why there is such a large gap between the top two responses, gas has 904 but milk has 455. I wonder why cars and used cars are listed separately. I wonder why some products were classified as food or not food. For example dog food, pet food, and oil are not counted as food products, but shampoo is counted as food. I’m surprised that only 22 people responded “everything” since because of inflation that’s very true.

3.  Inflation affects everyone. In the US minimum wage has not been increasing appropriately with inflation, so increasing prices impact everyone.

4. “What has gotten the most expensive?”

raw_comment:
In this weeks graph, I notice that many people were surveyed asking what they think has increased in price this past year. Gas is the most popular one followed by milk, meat and other food essentials. I wonder how much the prices have increased in all of these products. I also wonder if the increase is a result of COVID or something else. This relates to me as I have noticed an increase. I just got my license and in the year I have had it I have been able to notice a huge price increase in gas. This relates to my community as many of the items on this list are essentials. 
"Prices Increase, Income Decrease"

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graph shows the Feb. 2022 responses to the survey question:  Name specific products and services whose higher prices have stood out to them over the past year.  

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?”, “What do you wonder?"  and “How will this affect you and your community?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in this graph. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included this graph and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, April 1 with moderation on Wednesday, April 6.  The topic – biodiversity.  Keep noticing and wondering.

raw_comment:
In this graph, I notice that there is no real limit to what counts as a "product", and this even branched to entire services, such as "mcdonald's" and "dollar store".  Similar products may even be repeated, such as "Chicken", "chicken breast," and "poultry", rather than be attributed and organized into a single word. This indicates that this may be gathering specific personal opinion and word choice by people as well.

I wonder if the data organized this way intentionally, and why? Was this meant as a social experiment or as a means of creating an example of crowdsourcing data?

This is representative of products that many already believed may be unreasonably increasing in value, and there are many different topics that people in my community may agree with, especially regarding something more recent and topical such as gas prices.The collection of data for this graph may very well have included my community as well, which at that point would directly include an concern their own opinions, making them more involved with the issue.

raw_comment:
I notice that the data is organized by amount of responses per item, shown by large/small text. Gas has the largest text size with 904 responses, while shampoo is one of the smallest text sizes with 7 responses. They are also organized by type of item, as the food items are in orange and the random objects are in grey. Shampoo, however, is possibly a mistake because it is shown in orange in the graph yet it is an object.

I wonder where the sample was taken. Is it countrywide? Worldwide? How would the data change if the location(s) of the samples changed as well?

I think this impacts me and my community by making us more conscious about where we are spending our money. There are basic necessities towards the bottom of the list. Hygiene products are lower on the list than cigarettes; what does that say about our community?

Headline: 
What's the Word on our Spending?

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I noticed that most of these items are things that we use everyday. Also, the most popular item that people have noticed that the price has increased is gas. This is important because we all use gas everyday to get to and from places. Also, most of the items involved food. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why the prices of these specific items are increasing and not other items. Also, I wonder if these prices will continue to rise or when they will stop rising. Lastly, I wonder how or if there is any way that we can bring these prices down. 
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This impacts me and my community because I use these products everyday too. Even though I do not pay for my own groceries, I know that these product’s prices have increased. On top of that, since I can now drive and I pay for my own gas, I know that gas prices have increased a lot. 
4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.
In this graph, we see a list of words/things in which people have seen changes in an increase in price within the last year. The words that involve food are color coded in orange and the non food items are color coded in gray. A catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea would be “Items that have increased in price”
